facts.statement: British paleontologist David M. Martill purchased the holotype specimen directly at the mine site in January 2017.
facts.quote: The specimen was purchased directly at the mine site by British palaeontologist David M. Martill in January 2017

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists only of fragmented jaws.
facts.quote: and consists only of the pterosaur's fragmented jaws

facts.statement: Xericeps lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Xericeps is an extinct genus of alanqid pterosaur from the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: Researchers believe Xericeps lived between 93.9 and 113.0 million years ago during the Albian to Cenomanian ages.
facts.quote: It is believed that Xericeps lived in the mid-Cretaceous period around the Albian–Cenomanian ages (93.9–113.0 Ma)

facts.statement: Xericeps was a medium-sized pterosaur that lacked teeth.
facts.quote: Xericeps is a medium-sized edentulous (toothless) pterosaur

facts.statement: Xericeps likely had a wingspan near the lower end of the 3 to 8 meter range typical for medium-sized pterosaurs.
facts.quote: The term 'medium-sized', in the context of pterosaurs, is generally used to describe pterosaurs with a wingspan of 3–8 metres, and it is likely that Xericeps was nearer the lower end of this range

facts.statement: The upturned jaw of Xericeps has a curved occluding surface when viewed from the side.
facts.quote: The jaw is upturned, with the occluding surface curved in lateral view

facts.statement: A pair of ridges on the dorsal surface of the jaw symphysis resembles features found in Alanqa and Argentinadraco.
facts.quote: On the dorsal surface of the mandibular symphysis are a pair of ridges, similar to those seen in Alanqa and Argentinadraco

facts.statement: A 2021 study classified Xericeps as a chaoyangopterid closely related to Argentinadraco.
facts.quote: A 2021 study focused on Aerotitan recovered Xericeps as a chaoyangopterid closely related to Argentinadraco

facts.statement: Subsequent analyses consistently place Xericeps within the family Alanqidae.
facts.quote: Both Xericeps and Argentinadraco have since been consistently recovered as members of Alanqidae

facts.statement: Some sources classify Xericeps within the family Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: familia: Azhdarchidae

facts.statement: Martill and colleagues classified Xericeps within the clade Neoazhdarchia based on the presence of foramina in the jaw.
facts.quote: Martill et al. clasificaron por tanto a Xericeps en el clado Neoazhdarchia

facts.statement: The holotype jaw fragment measures 173 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: La pieza de mandíbula tiene una longitud de 173 milímetros

facts.statement: The shape of the ridges on Xericeps' jaw differs from those of Alanqa, a pterosaur from the same geological layers.
facts.quote: La mandíbula también difiere en la forma de las crestas de Alanqa, un pterosaurio de las mismas capas geológicas

facts.statement: Five pairs of elongated holes, serving as openings for venous ducts, are located along the lower edges of the jaw.
facts.quote: A lo largo de los bordes inferiores hay cinco pares de agujeros (forámenes) alargados, aberturas para conductos venosos

facts.statement: Xericeps inhabited a subtropical alluvial plain characterized by rivers, deltas, and swampy lakes.
facts.quote: Xericeps vivía en una llanura aluvial con clima subtropical, consistente en una serie de ríos, deltas y lagos pantanosos

facts.statement: The habitat of Xericeps was shared with large theropod dinosaurs like Spinosaurus and Carcharodontosaurus, as well as the sauropod Rebbachisaurus.
facts.quote: Este hábitat también era frecuentado por grandes dinosaurios terópodos como Spinosaurus y Carcharodontosaurus, y el extraño saurópodo Rebbachisaurus

facts.statement: The exact diet of Xericeps remains uncertain, though relatives like Alanqa appear to have specialized in hunting hard-shelled mollusks.
facts.quote: Martill et al. no llegaron a establecer dieta del animal con certeza, pero muchos de sus parientes cercanos eran depredadores terrestres de animales pequeños, y Alanqa en particular parece haber sido un depredador especializado de moluscos de concha dura

facts.statement: Xericeps is known solely from its holotype specimen, which was originally described in 2017.
facts.quote: Xericeps es conocido solo a partir de su espécimen holotipo, descrito originalmente en 2017

facts.statement: The name Xericeps combines the Greek word for 'dry' referencing the Sahara Desert and the Latin suffix for 'head', alluding to its forceps-like beak.
facts.quote: El nombre Xericeps proviene del término griego - xero - que significa "seco", en referencia al desierto del Sahara en el cual se hallaron sus fósiles, y el sufijo latino ~ ceps derivado de caput que significa "cabeza", en alusión al pico de la criatura, que recordaría a un fórceps

facts.statement: The fossil material represents an adult animal.
facts.quote: El material óseo corresponde a un animal adulto

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Xericeps as Neoazhdarchia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Neoazhdarchia

facts.statement: The time range for Xericeps is recorded as the Cenomanian, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen of Xericeps was discovered by local mine workers at Aferdou N'Chaft in southeastern Morocco near the Algerian border.
rejected.quote: The holotype specimen, FSAC-KK-10700, was discovered by local mine workers at Aferdou N'Chaft, a small mesa near the oasis village of Hassi el Begaa in the Errachidia Province in southeastern Morocco on the Algerian border
